title: eszik and iszik: Two Special Verbs

sections.title: The -ik verbs you eat and drink with
sections.content: Back in A1 you met the tip that -ik verbs like dolgozik swap the regular -ok/-ek/-ök for -om/-em/-öm in the "I" form — dolgozom, not dolgozok. eszik ("to eat") and iszik ("to drink") are exactly that kind of verb, and you've already used eszem and iszom once, in a Unit 13 story. Now you get their full present tense.

items.spanish: Reggel kenyeret eszem és teát iszom.
items.english: In the morning I eat bread and drink tea.

items.spanish: Mit eszel és mit iszol ma?
items.english: What are you eating and drinking today?

sections.content: iszik looks like it should follow front-vowel endings because of the i, but it actually takes back-vowel endings throughout (iszom, not iszem; isztok, not isztek) — one of the handful of Hungarian verbs where the eye and the ear disagree. The infinitives are also irregular and worth knowing again here: enni (to eat) and inni (to drink), both already familiar from A1.
